BatteryOperationMode.description:
The current operation mode of the battery.

 * `SELF_RELIANCE`: The battery optimizes itself to maximize self-consumption: it charges from solar surplus if available, discharges to cover household load, and the household only imports from the grid when both fall short. Excess solar may still be exported to the grid. This is the default mode on most batteries.
 * `TIME_OF_USE`: The battery optimizes itself against an electricity price schedule configured in the manufacturer's app: it charges when electricity is cheap and discharges when it is expensive. Energy may flow to or from the grid depending on prices and the user's settings.
 * `IMPORT_FOCUS`: Steers the battery to charge from any available source. Use this to increase household demand, fill the battery ahead of high prices, or support other optimization strategies.
 * `EXPORT_FOCUS`: Steers the battery to discharge: powers the household first and exports any excess to the grid where allowed. Use this to decrease household demand by releasing stored energy or support grid shortfalls.
 * `IDLE`: Holds the current charge level: the battery neither charges nor discharges. Use this to pass solar production through to the household or grid, or to hold the battery's charge for later.
 * `UNKNOWN`: Reported when Enode cannot map the manufacturer's current mode to one of the modes above. This value cannot be set; the battery can usually be moved out of it by setting one of the modes above.

All modes set a **target behavior**. Actual behavior can vary with the device's configuration, the user's settings in the manufacturer's app, reserve limits, and local grid rules.

ActionState.description:
The real-time status of an action executed on a target. 

 * `PENDING`: The initial state. Enode is actively sending commands and monitoring the target for changes. 
 * `CONFIRMED`: Successful transition of the target to the desired state. 
 * `FAILED`: The target did not respond to the action before timing out. Enode has ceased sending additional commands. 
 * `CANCELLED`: A required precondition was not met during the action's timeout window or another action has been sent to the target, overriding this one.

type.description:
A machine-readable high level error category.

 * `NO_RESPONSE`: The device did not react to our commands within the action's timeout window.  
 * `FAILED_PRECONDITION`: The device did not meet all required preconditions for this action to be executed during the action's timeout window. 
 * `UNNECESSARY`: The action was not carried out given that the device was already in the desired state. 
 * `CONFLICT`: A newer action for this device, or for a device paired with it, has replaced this action. This action is now abandoned.  
 * `REQUESTED_CANCELLATION`: This action was cancelled by request of the controlling owner. The controlling owner may refer to another Enode entity which initiated the command, such as a schedule or smart override. 
 * `NOT_FOUND`: The device was deleted while the action was `PENDING`.

ChargerPowerDeliveryState.description:
The current state of power delivery between the vehicle and charger.

 * `UNKNOWN`: The state of power delivery is currently unknown. 
 * `UNPLUGGED`: The vehicle is not connected to the charger. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:INITIALIZING`: The charging station is preparing to deliver power to the vehicle. It is expected for this state to shortly transition into PLUGGED_IN:CHARGING. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:CHARGING`: The charger is actively delivering power to the vehicle, causing the battery level to increase. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:STOPPED`: The vehicle is plugged in, but the charger has been stopped. It is possible to transition into a charging state by sending a start command.
 * `PLUGGED_IN:NO_POWER`: The charger attempted to initialize charging, however no external power was accepted by the vehicle. It is not possible to transition into a charging state with a remote command until there is some user intervention to resolve the issue. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:FAULT`: A malfunction in the charging process is preventing power from being delivered. Possible causes include a charging cable not being properly locked, extreme temperatures, or malfunctions in either the charging station or the vehicle's internal system. It is not possible to transition into a charging state with a remote command until there is some user intervention to resolve the issue.
 * `PLUGGED_IN:DISCHARGING`: The charger is actively discharging by giving power to the home/grid, causing the battery level to decrease.

HvacMode.description:
The current state of the HVAC unit.

 * `OFF`: The HVAC unit is turned off.
 * `AUTO`: The HVAC unit will try to maintain the given setpoint by alternating between cooling and heating based on the ambient temperature
 * `COOL`: The HVAC unit will only cool to the given setpoint.
 * `HEAT`: The HVAC unit will only heat to the given setpoint
 * `null`: The mode of the HVAC unit is currently not available from the vendor or not supported by enode.

VehiclePowerDeliveryState.description:
The current state of power delivery between the vehicle and charger.

 * `UNKNOWN`: The state of power delivery is currently unknown. 
 * `UNPLUGGED`: The vehicle is not connected to the charger. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:INITIALIZING`: The charging station is preparing to deliver power to the vehicle. It is expected for this state to shortly transition into PLUGGED_IN:CHARGING. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:CHARGING`: The vehicle is actively receiving power from the charger, causing the battery level to increase. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:COMPLETE`: The charging process has finished and the vehicle's battery has reached the target charge limit. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:STOPPED`: The charging process has been intentionally stopped by either the vehicle or the charger. The vehicle is still plugged in and waiting for the charging process to resume. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:NO_POWER`: The vehicle attempted to initialize charging, however no external power was available. It is not possible to transition into a charging state with a remote command until there is some user intervention to resolve the issue. 
 * `PLUGGED_IN:FAULT`: A malfunction in the charging process is preventing power from being delivered. Possible causes include a charging cable not being properly locked, extreme temperatures, or malfunctions in either the charging station or the vehicle's internal system. It is not possible to transition into a charging state with a remote command until there is some user intervention to resolve the issue.
 * `PLUGGED_IN:DISCHARGING`: The vehicle is actively discharging by giving power to the home/grid, causing the battery level to decrease.

status.description:
Ready-state of the Vendor.

  * `READY`: We are not aware of any issues with this Vendor.
  * `ELEVATED_ERROR_RATE`: Performance is degraded. Data updates may arrive slower than usual, and actions may fail.
  * `OUTAGE`: Connectivity to this Vendor is broken. Data updates and actions are failing until this is resolved.
  * `MAINTENANCE`: Planned maintenance at the Vendor. Data updates and actions may be unavailable until it completes.

This follows the incidents and in-progress maintenance windows we publish on [our status page](https://status.enode.com) and may lag them. A maintenance window that has been announced but has not started does not change this field. It reports only what we have detected and declared, so `READY` means we are not aware of an issue, not that we have confirmed the Vendor is healthy. It is informational: whether a user can link is `linkingStatus`.

  * `MAINTENANCE`: The Vendor is temporarily unavailable for linking due to planned maintenance. We will show a planned maintenance screen in Link UI and not let the user attempt to link with the Vendor.

Returned timestamps encode the local wall-clock bucket start with a `Z` suffix; for example, local midnight is returned as `00:00:00Z` for every offset. Treat these timestamps as bucket labels, not the UTC instants when the local periods began. 

For `QUARTER_HOUR`, `HALF_HOUR`, and `HOUR`, samples are shifted by the offset before assignment to the UTC-aligned response grid, and returned timestamps are not shifted back. A non-zero offset can therefore move values between response buckets. 

Deprecated: this is a fixed offset, not a time zone, and does not account for daylight-saving changes. Omit it to use UTC bucketing.
